description:
Pete Hegseth survived an impeachment push in the House, then got called out by a soldier guarding the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier 🗳️

On Tuesday, November 10, the House voted 211 to 204 to send eight articles of impeachment against the Secretary of Defense to the Judiciary Committee, effectively killing the effort without ever voting on the merits. The vote fell along party lines, with one exception: Thomas Massie, the Republican who forced it.

Massie has spent months clashing with Trump. After he teamed up with Democrats to force the release of the Epstein files, Trump endorsed his primary challenger, former Navy SEAL Ed Gallrein, and Hegseth traveled to Kentucky to campaign against Massie. Gallrein won. With Democrats set to control both chambers in the next Congress, Massie used his final months in office to make House Republicans choose between standing behind Hegseth and holding him accountable. 

They stood behind him, and Hegseth dismissed the effort as political revenge from
title: A Tomb Guard Just Yelled at Pete Hegseth
